name: application-command-bar-breadcrumb
title: Command Bar Breadcrumb
description: A breadcrumb trail where one segment doubles as a dropdown trigger, revealing sibling pages or projects at that level without leaving the trail.
useWhen: Users regularly switch between sibling items at one level of a hierarchy (projects, workspaces, folders) and jumping there directly from the breadcrumb saves a trip up and back down.
The navigation context is deep enough that a breadcrumb is already warranted, and at least one level has several siblings worth surfacing.
avoidWhen: The hierarchy is shallow or each level has only one path — a plain `breadcrumbs` trail is simpler and avoids implying interactivity that isn't needed.
Sibling switching is rare — a dedicated switcher (like a project picker) elsewhere in the UI may be more discoverable than an interactive breadcrumb segment.
responsiveBehavior: Segments wrap via flex-wrap on narrow viewports rather than truncating; the open sibling list is left-anchored to its trigger and keeps a fixed width regardless of trail length.
accessibility: The interactive segment is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-haspopup="listbox", distinguishing it from the plain <a> segments around it.
The sibling list uses role="listbox"/role="option" with aria-selected marking the current item, plus a visible checkmark.
The final segment carries aria-current="page" to mark the active location, per breadcrumb convention.

variants.title: Open sibling menu
variants.description: A four-level breadcrumb trail with the second segment ('Design System') expanded into an open dropdown of sibling projects, the current one checked.
accessibility: The interactive segment's aria-expanded and aria-haspopup mark it as distinct from the static link segments.

variants.title: Open sibling menu (Dark)
variants.description: Command bar breadcrumb adapted for dark surfaces, including the active-segment highlight and open dropdown.
accessibility: Segment text, separators, and the open dropdown all meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark background.
